raw: | A mapping rooted below an array (`root choices/message`) builds a project mxbuild rejects with **CE0243** "The mapping used to return a value of type 'X', but now returns a value of type 'List of X'" | Such a mapping yields ONE OBJECT PER ITEM, so the import activity must bind a list. `mappingRootIsList` answered from the JSON **structure**'s root element, which for `root choices/message` is the document root — an Object — so it reported a single object. The mapping DOCUMENT is correct and cannot decide this: Studio Pro's own `OpenAI_API.IM_OpenAI` stores `MaxOccurs 1` on exactly that root (verified against the fixture), so list-ness lives only in the root's PATH | `mdl/executor/cmd_microflows_builder_calls.go` (`mappingRootIsList`, `mappingRootPathCrossesArray`) | An array contributes a marker segment for its item, so **any `(Object)`/`(Array)`/`(Wrapper)` segment after the first** means the root sits inside an array: `(Object)|choices|(Object)|message` and `(Array)|(Object)` are lists, `(Object)|data` is not. Skip the first segment — it is always the document's own root marker. Keep the existing structure-root and MaxOccurs checks as the fallback for XML-schema and message-definition mappings, which carry no JsonPath. **Found by building an app and running `mx check` on it** — every unit test in the package passed while this was broken, and so did the whole mapping fixture round-trip suite, because the defect is in the CALLER of the mapping, not the mapping. The wider lesson is the one #294 taught: a mapping that serializes correctly and builds cleanly can still do nothing at run time, so a mapping feature is not proven until data has moved through it. Repro + assertions: `mdl-examples/bug-tests/mapping-runtime-proof.mdl` and its `.test.mdl`, run with `mxcli run --local --test-endpoint` + `mxcli test --attach`. Tests `mdl/executor/cmd_microflows_nested_root_cardinality_test.go`. Follow-up to ako/mxcli#267 |
